Question: Some candies are distributed among \(x\) children. If each child receives 3 candies, 5 candies remain. If each child is allocated 4 candies, the last child receives fewer than 4 candies (at least 1 candy). What is the maximum value of \(x\)?
Solution: There are \(3x+5\) candies in total. The last child receives \(3x+5-4(x-1)=9-x\) candies. Thus, \(1\leq9-x<4\), giving \(5<x\leq8\), so the maximum value of \(x\) is 8.
